data.title: Texas Jury Convicts Indian National in $150,000,000 Elder Fraud Scheme
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have secured a conviction against an Indian national for laundering proceeds from a massive call center scam that targeted elderly US victims.

Bhavesh Kumar Thakkar, 45, was found guilty on two counts of wire fraud and money laundering after acting as a US-based coordinator who received and moved cash and gold from victims, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas.

“The fraud proceeds were obtained by call center scammers based in India.”

Thakkar worked with co-defendants to ship funds to Los Angeles and New York before laundering overseas and was tied directly to more than $150 million in fraud proceeds.

Two co-defendants already received prison sentences of 97 months and 63 months, while a third awaits sentencing.

Says U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons,

“Foreign actors, both abroad and here in the United States, cannot be allowed to target Americans, especially our most vulnerable citizens. Many victims lose a significant portion of their life savings to these scammers, leaving victims vulnerable and hopeless. When we find them, we will do all we can to take from them the same sense of freedom and comfort they stole from their victims.”

The FBI and Granite Shoals Police Department investigated the case.

data.title: Oracle Health Breach Exposes Nearly 20,000,000 Patient Records Across Up To 80 US Hospitals – Names, SSNs and Medical Data at Risk
data.description:
A major health-tech firm has exposed the personal and medical data of nearly 20 million people after a hacker broke into outdated hospital servers.

Oracle Health, which runs systems formerly operated by Cerner, confirmed that an unauthorized person reached two legacy Cerner servers that had not yet moved to Oracle Cloud, reports HIPAA Journal.

Cerner is a major health information technology company and electronic health record (EHR) platform used by more than 27,000 healthcare facilities across over 35 countries. Oracle acquired Cerner in 2022 in a $28.4 billion mega deal and merged the firm into Oracle Health.

State filings place the intrusion in a window from January 22nd, 2025, to April 1st, 2025.

Oracle Health says it became aware of the breach on or around March 7th, 2025.

The Texas Attorney General reveals 2,992,244 Texans are affected, with Oregon listing 1,978,661, South Carolina 283,903 and Washington 69,238.

Bloomberg puts the nationwide figure near 20 million patients, impacting as many as 80 hospitals.

Stolen data reportedly includes names, Social Security numbers, medical record numbers, diagnoses, medications, test results, medical images and physician names.

A hacker demanded ransom to keep the files from being published.

Oracle Health has said its current systems and Oracle Cloud infrastructure were not hit.

Says Oracle Health,

“We are writing to inform you that, on or around February 20, 2025, we became aware of a cybersecurity event involving unauthorized access to some amount of your Cerner data that was on an old legacy server not yet migrated to the Oracle Cloud.”

data.title: Arizona Sues TikTok, Alleging App Was Engineered To Get Kids Addicted and Hide the Harms
data.description:
A state is suing one of the world’s biggest social media apps over allegations that it was built to get children and teens addicted while hiding the toll on their mental health.

The lawsuit accuses TikTok and parent company ByteDance of using infinite scrolling, auto-play, push notifications and appearance-altering filters to keep minors on the app so the company can profit from their data, says Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes.

“TikTok touts its supposed safety measures to convince parents that this product is safe for young people. But behind the company’s marketing is a platform engineered to exploit the vulnerabilities of developing brains, pushing Arizona kids toward compulsive use, harmful content, and dangerous behaviors while failing to protect them from adults who use the social media platform to groom or solicit minors. It’s unconscionable.”

The complaint alleges TikTok downplayed or failed to disclose risks including depression, anxiety, disordered eating and self-harm. It also alleges the company knowingly allows children under 13 on the app despite publicly claiming to bar them.

“The complaint further alleges that TikTok’s recommendation algorithms expose minors to increasingly extreme, harmful, or age?inappropriate content and that TikTok’s content?moderation practices are inadequate to block much of the dangerous material on the platform.”

The state alleges TikTok’s 60-minute screen time limit for teens was known not to cut their use.

A TikTok spokesperson denies the allegations, reports KJZZ.

Says the spokesperson,

“This lawsuit relies on misleading and inaccurate claims and deliberately ignores the concrete safety measures TikTok has voluntarily implemented to support the well-being of our community. We will vigorously defend against these claims.”

data.title: $2,400 Abruptly Drained From Georgia Woman’s Bank Account After She Purchases $2 Bottle of Water From Street Vendor via Zelle: Report
data.description:
A Georgia driver says she has lost $2,400 after trying to buy a $2 bottle of water from a street seller in Atlanta.

Monet Swann says a young man selling water walked up to her car window on 10th Street near Techwood Drive in Midtown on October 1st, reports 11Alive.

Swann says she agreed to pay through Zelle by scanning a QR code and screen-sharing what she believed was a $2 payment.

Instead, she says $1,200 left her account. Swann says,

“So, I screenshared and authorized a two-dollar purchase from Zelle and unfortunately, he took $1,200 from me.”

She says the seller also somehow accessed her Apple Pay account and pulled an additional $1,200, bringing the total loss she allegedly incurred to $2,400.

Swann says she notified her bank about the transactions in an effort to get back the money but her fraud claim have been denied. According to 11Alive, Swann hopes that her experience can serve as a cautionary tale to others in Atlanta who encounter water boys.

“Water boys could scam you. If they even try to approach you, I would say just keep walking. You can’t even be good to people in this world anymore even if you do have a good heart because I always tell myself, as long as you’re good to others, the blessings will come your way.”

No arrests have been reported.

data.title: Crypto Wallet Ledger Now Lets Users Borrow Stablecoins Against Their Bitcoin Without Giving Up Self-Custody
data.description:
Crypto hardware wallet maker Ledger is rolling out a new feature that lets users borrow stablecoins against their Bitcoin (BTC) without giving up custody of their assets.

The new Crypto Loan feature lets Ledger Wallet users deposit wrapped Bitcoin as collateral and borrow the dollar-pegged stablecoins USDC or USDT directly inside the app, says Ledger.

The service is powered by the on-chain lending network Morpho and plugged into the app through Yield.xyz.

Users can post either cbBTC or wBTC as collateral and keep their Bitcoin exposure for the life of the loan instead of selling their holdings.

Says Ledger in its latest release notes,

“Morpho is an onchain credit network; the smart contracts govern every interaction, and your collateral stays on-chain rather than sitting on someone else’s balance sheet.”

Every step of the loan, from the first approval to repayment and withdrawal, has to be confirmed on the screen of a Ledger hardware device, which shows each contract function in plain language.

The app also tracks each loan’s loan-to-value (LTV) ratio and lets users add collateral, repay, borrow more or withdraw at any time, with an option to simulate a loan before committing.

Ledger is also adding direct access to Morpho’s lending markets and curated vaults for depositing, borrowing and earning across Ethereum (ETH) and major layer-2 networks.

The company says interest rates are variable, liquidation risks apply and Crypto Loan is subject to country availability.

Ledger says it acts only as a technology provider and does not give financial advice.

data.title: Billionaire Ray Dalio Warns China and Japan Could Pull Back From US Treasuries As 10-Year Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
data.description:
Billionaire investor Ray Dalio is warning that the US Treasury market is exposed to a drop in demand from China and Japan.

The Bridgewater Associates founder says the US depends on foreign capital for about a third of its debt, with much of that money coming from Japan and China, reports Bloomberg.

Dalio tells Bloomberg Television that geopolitical tensions mean China no longer wants to keep adding US debt to its holdings.

He says Japan has lent “a lot of money” that it now wants to bring back home.

Since the start of the year, China and Japan have reduced their holdings of US treasuries by a combined $198.7 billion. Japan, which is the largest foreign creditor to the US, held $1.1039 trillion in US treasuries as of July. China is the third-largest foreign creditor to the US and as of July held $618 billion in US treasuries.

Dalio also repeated his warning that the US could face a debt crisis within three years.

His comments come as a global bond selloff pushes government borrowing costs to multi-year highs.

The yield on the 10-year US Treasury is hovering around 5.3%, a level not seen since 2002.

Inflation, fiscal spending and resilient economic growth have weakened demand for bonds around the world.

Bond prices have kept falling this week, extending a slide that has lasted for months.

data.title: Banks and Other Lenders Seize 42% More US Homes Than a Year Ago As Texas and Florida Lead the Nation in Repossessions
data.description:
Banks and other lenders are taking back far more American homes than they were a year ago.

Lenders completed foreclosures on 5,794 US properties in August, a 42% jump from August of 2025 and a 22% rise from July, says real estate data firm ATTOM.

Texas accounted for 1,835 of those repossessions, more than three times the 589 recorded in California.

North Carolina, Arizona and Alabama followed with 356, 296 and 286 completed foreclosures respectively.

Houston saw more bank repossessions than any other major metro area with 448, followed by Dallas with 402 and San Antonio with 256.

In total, 40,277 properties nationwide received a foreclosure filing in August, including default notices, scheduled auctions and bank repossessions.

That figure is up 13% from a year earlier.

Lenders started the foreclosure process on 25,894 homes during the month, 7% more than a year ago.

South Carolina posted the worst foreclosure rate in the country, with one filing for every 1,547 housing units, followed by Nevada and Florida.

Says ATTOM chief executive Rob Barber,

“August’s data shows that foreclosure activity continues to trend above year-ago levels, particularly in completed foreclosures, which saw a notable annual increase. While some homeowners are still facing financial challenges, overall foreclosure volumes remain well below historical norms and the broader housing market continues to demonstrate resilience.”

ATTOM says overall foreclosure activity is still below pre-pandemic levels.

data.title: China Splurges $2,895,995,400 on Gold in One Month As Global Central Banks Gobble Up 170 Tons of the Yellow Metal Year-to-Date
data.description:
China’s central bank added another 20 tons of gold in August as central banks worldwide kept buying.

The People’s Bank of China has now bought gold for 22 straight months, lifting its year-to-date total to 80 tons and its official stockpile to about 2,387 tons, roughly 9% of its reserves, reports the World Gold Council.

Global central banks reported 39 tons of net purchases in August and 170 tons so far this year. Year-to-date, China has added 80 tons of gold to its central bank reserves.

“China’s official gold reserves now stand at 9% of total reserves, or around 2,387 tons.”

Poland remains the top buyer year-to-date after adding 8 tons in August for a 2026 total of 98 tons.

Its holdings now sit at 648 tons as Warsaw works toward a 700-ton target.

Uzbekistan bought 8 tons and Kazakhstan 7 tons, leaving gold at about 90% and 79% of their reserves, respectively. Year-to-date gold purchases by the two countries’ central banks now stands at 50 tons and 36 tons, respectively.

The Czech National Bank added 2 tons and Turkey bought 3 tons after three months of net sales.

Says Marissa Salim, senior research lead for Asia-Pacific at the World Gold Council,

“Global central banks remain on pace with gold accumulation this August, with reported net buying totalling 39t.”

Meanwhile, Russia sold another 6 tons in August. The Central Bank of Jordan also sold 3 tons over the same period.

Gold is trading at $4,105 an ounce at time of writing.

data.title: Former Engineer Gets 32 Months Prison for Hacking Employer and Demanding Bitcoin (BTC) Ransom
data.description:
A disgruntled former core infrastructure engineer at a New Jersey industrial company sabotaged the firm’s computer network and extorted employees with a large Bitcoin (BTC) ransom demand.

The U.S. Department of Justice says 59-year-old Missouri man Daniel Rhyne pleaded guilty to a two-count information that charged him with extortion in relation to a threat to cause damage to a protected computer and intentional damage to a protected computer.

In or around November 2023, Rhyne took steps to execute a scheme to hack his employer’s computer network and extort the firm into paying a ransom.

The engineer initiated unauthorized remote desktop sessions and scheduled tasks to delete network administrator accounts, change passwords, and shut down multiple servers.

“On November 25, 2023, Rhyne sent an extortion email to Victim-1 employees in which he threatened to continue shutting down Victim-1 servers unless and until he received approximately 20 Bitcoin, which, at the time, was valued at approximately $750,000.”

At time of writing, 20 Bitcoin is worth about $1.667 million.

He pleaded guilty on April 1st, 2026, in Trenton federal court before U.S. District Judge Michael A. Shipp.

Shipp sentenced Rhyne on October 5th, 2026, to 32 months in prison.

The FBI’s Newark Field Office and FBI Kansas City investigated the case, which was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert Taj Moore of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark.

data.title: Connecticut Resident Sentenced to Eight Years for Masterminding $55,000,000 Check Fraud Ring
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have secured an eight-year prison sentence for the leader of a scheme that stole thousands of checks from U.S. Postal Service collection boxes and deposited millions in altered funds.

Michael Edwards, 31, of Bridgeport, Connecticut, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge John G. Koeltl in the Southern District of New York, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

The scheme ran from January 2022 through July 2024 and involved more than 2,600 stolen checks, with intended losses exceeding $55 million, of which more than $18 million was deposited.

Edwards worked with others to obtain postal keys that provided access to collection boxes in affluent Manhattan neighborhoods.

After stealing checks, Edwards and his co-conspirators altered the names of the payees and, in some cases, the amounts written on the checks.

Prosecutors also say Edwards helped recruit people willing to provide their bank account information and oversaw the deposit of millions of dollars in fraudulently altered checks into accounts across Connecticut, Florida, Pennsylvania and South Carolina.

Says U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald,

“For more than two years, Michael Edwards criminally utilized the U.S. mail system to steal millions of dollars from Americans who rely on it by obtaining postal keys, stealing thousands of checks from the mail, washing those checks, and depositing the fraudulent checks or posting them for sale on Telegram. Even after his arrest, Edwards kept operating his illicit business on Telegram and obstructed justice by deleting his Telegram posts. Today’s prison sentence is indicative of the result awaiting those who breach the U.S. mail system to steal from everyday Americans.”

On top of the prison sentence, Edwards received three years of supervised release and was ordered to forfeit $18,840,084.45 while paying restitution.
